messages:
jamie: FYI i'm prototyping a 'claim' flow for service/api keys used by shared infra (eg. model-proxy). idea: keys can be bound to a project OR remain org-shared but projects can claim a read-only view for billing/debug. want quick feedback on visibility + audit surface.
leo: high level sounds OK. two immediate concerns: 1) 'claiming' shouldn't transfer ownership or permissions 2) claims must be revocable and audited.
anya: agreed. semantics: claim = metadata link, not permission grant. real enforcement still by key's ACLs. viewers get a Claim record resource. we can reuse existing "resource_claim" RBAC verb.
ops: for debugging, teams want to see which service used a key (hostname, deploy-id). exposing deploy-id is sensitive. propose a scrubbed view: show service_type + public_label + first_seen. full details require "view_sensitive_key_meta" permission.
jamie: good call. propose API surface: POST /keys/:id/claim {project_id, reason, public_label?} DELETE /keys/:id/claim -> revoke. GET /keys/:id/claim returns claim record conditioned on permission.
leo: caching note: don't cache claim lookup longer than 1m in gateways; ops needs near-real-time revoke. maybe gateway caches 30s, internal services can use longer.
anya: audit: emit ClaimCreated/ClaimRevoked events with actor, project_id, reason, and redacted metadata if necessary. retention per org policy.
security-bot: policy-scan: finds 2 items: (A) potential info-leak: deploy-id in claim events visible to non-privileged listeners, (B) revocation race: cached gateways may allow 30s window of access post-revoke. recommendations: redact deploy-id in events unless consumer opts-in; reduce cache TTL for high-sensitivity keys. :warning:
jamie: we'll redact by default and allow opt-in by creating an "expose_sensitive_metadata" flag on the claim that requires admin approval. revocation window is acceptable if documented SLAs state up to 30s. can add push invalidation for critical keys.
ops: push invalidation support would be great. add endpoint POST /keys/:id/invalidate-caches that triggers immediate invalidate hooks to gateways. require admin or key-owner role.
leo: RBAC modeling: treat Claim as a first-class resource. permissions: create: claim:create on key resource; read: claim:view; revoke: claim:revoke. separate permission claim:expose_sensitive to set expose_sensitive_metadata.
anya: migration: existing org-shared keys have no claims. default behavior: no auto-claim. we'll provide bulk-claim UI for infra owners. also an audit-only mode to backfill historical usage into claim-like records for billing.
jamie: small sample of enforcement pseudo:
```
// check read of claim record
func canViewClaim(requester, claim) bool {
  if requester.is_org_admin { return true }
  if authz.HasPermission(requester, "claim:view", claim.key_resource) { return true }
  return false
}
```

ops: telemetry: internal logs include claim.project_id but external billing export must use public_label unless expose_sensitive_metadata=true. GA export must never contain deploy-id.
devx-bot: noted. created task INFRA-547 to add cache-invalidate endpoint.
jamie: decision summary for RFC follow-up: 1) add Claim resource and claim APIs (create/read/delete) 2) Claim = metadata pointer only, no transfer of ACLs 3) permission model with granular verbs (view, create, revoke, expose_sensitive) 4) redact sensitive fields by default; opt-in requires admin approval 5) short gateway cache (30s) + optional push invalidation 6) audit events for create/revoke; backfill mode for billing. i'll draft RFC with endpoints, schema, and migration steps.
anya: please include the exact event schema in RFC. ops: include runbooks for revoke/push-invalidate.
jamie: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:
